summary: The adversarial round of Phase 2 at the audited code head be5b22394398e0c0c7117a5e347674f64e9721dd added 13 cases in two files. Eleven cases pass on the shipped tree, and two cases fail on real product defects, so the phase does not pass. K2a: a rapid mode-switch storm shows the red sound-error alert while the narration plays, because reader.tsx lines 243-256 treat every rejected play() as a failure and a browser aborts the pending play with AbortError when the mode switch writes a new src. S4b: a one-page book never records its finish, because the done write at reader.tsx line 202 needs book.pages.length > 1. The two failing cases live in apps/storytime/__tests__/look-adversarial-p2-defects.test.tsx as the Red proof for Green. The eleven passing cases live in apps/storytime/__tests__/look-adversarial-p2.test.tsx. Nine one-line mutants in a scratch copy were rejected by the cases. The role base is dd66da7e33d7a0dccce5ffb50bf8a449beb0265c, the HEAD at run start; the audited code head is be5b22394398e0c0c7117a5e347674f64e9721dd, and no look-track commit lies between the two heads.

blocking_findings: K2a [Major] a rapid mode-switch storm shows a false sound-error alert: apps/storytime/app/[locale]/st/[level]/[week]/reader.tsx lines 243-256. The playAudio helper attaches a catch to every rejected play() promise and calls setAudioFailed(true) with no check of the error name. A browser aborts the pending play promise with AbortError when the media load algorithm runs, and startListen, startMyTurn and startSlow each write a new src to the sentence audio (reader.tsx lines 307-347). The red alert therefore appears while the sound plays, and the child reads a failure that did not happen. The sibling screen already guards this case: decodable.tsx lines 244-274 hold the isAbortError helper and skip the alert for an aborted play (finding F120), and the reader clip path holds the same guard at reader.tsx lines 381-385. Action: Green reuses the isAbortError guard in playAudio, so an AbortError shows no alert and a real rejection still shows it. The Red case is apps/storytime/__tests__/look-adversarial-p2-defects.test.tsx (K2a).

S4b [Minor] a one-page book never records its finish: apps/storytime/app/[locale]/st/[level]/[week]/reader.tsx line 202. The done write runs only when book.pages.length > 1, so a book with one page writes no record at its last page and the Done badge of that card never appears. The decodable writes at its last page without a page-count condition (decodable.tsx line 225). This confirms the one-page-book finding of Review A at be5b22394. Action: Green writes the record when the reader reaches its last page, with no page-count condition. The Red case is apps/storytime/__tests__/look-adversarial-p2-defects.test.tsx (S4b).
nonblocking_findings: A browser gap for the UX browser review: the plaque has no nowrap rule and holds a max-width, but the plaque of the landscape block sets a fixed height of 40 px (app/look.css lines 821-831). A 60-character title at 568 x 320 needs more room than 40 px, so the title text can leave the plaque box. The browser gate row 3 measures a 60-character title at 390 x 844, 1024 x 768 and 844 x 390, and no row measures it at 320 x 568 or at 568 x 320. The case needs a browser measurement, not a jsdom case.

A browser gap for the UX browser review: the forced-colors palette and the 200 percent text zoom need a browser run. The jsdom cases pin the state signals that survive a forced palette (the sound button changes its label and its aria-pressed state, and the done badge keeps a stroked mark), and they pin the font stacks and the ground colours, but no case proves the painted palette under a forced palette.

The week parent speaker shows no message when its recording fails to load, and the song screen shows none either. The reader and the decodable show a role=alert message. The look phase does not name this surface, so the gap is recorded and not routed. apps/storytime/app/[locale]/st/[level]/[week]/speaker-button.tsx lines 29-34 swallow the play rejection.
